svg.title: The Cramér–Rao bound for the mean of a Gaussian
svg.desc: Left: log-likelihood curves for the mean of a Gaussian with known spread, for 1, 4 and 16 observations; the peak gets narrower as observations increase. Right: the variance of an estimate against the number of observations on logarithmic scales; the Cramér–Rao bound is a straight line falling as one over N, the sample mean sits exactly on it, the median stays a constant factor above it, and the region below the line is out of reach for unbiased estimators.
svg.text: dashed: the median stays above the bound
solid: the sample mean sits on the bound
likelihood of the mean for 1, 4 and 16 observations
Cramér–Rao: variance can't go below the line
Gaussian with known spread 1: the sharper the likelihood peak, the smaller the floor; the sample mean reaches it, the median does not
